title: Lopud Crowds by Month: When to Avoid Them in 2027
metaDescription: Lopud crowd levels month by month for 2027, with the quietest months, the busiest ferry and beach hours, and tips for avoiding day-trip crowds.
content:
## How Busy Is Lopud Month by Month?

Lopud is a car-free island of about 250 year-round residents in the Elaphiti archipelago. It lies about 10 nautical miles from Dubrovnik, and the ferry takes roughly 45–55 minutes. Crowds depend almost entirely on how many day-trippers arrive from Dubrovnik. Overnight guests are few, because the island has limited accommodation.

## Crowd Levels by Month

### January to March: Almost Empty
Lopud is nearly silent in winter. The ferry runs a reduced timetable, and most restaurants, beach bars and shops are closed. Quiet is guaranteed, but services are thin. Anyone staying overnight should confirm in advance that a restaurant and a grocery shop are open.

### April and May: Low Crowds, Services Returning
This is the best balance for avoiding people. Cafés and konobas reopen gradually, and the beaches are mostly empty on weekdays. The off-season ferry timetable stays in force until 28 May 2026, with departures from Dubrovnik at 10:00, 14:00, 16:30 and 20:00 Monday to Saturday. The 2027 dates are expected to follow a similar pattern, but check them with Jadrolinija. Occasional school groups and cruise-linked excursions create short midday peaks.

### June: Busy, but Manageable
Day-trip traffic builds steadily. The summer timetable starts at the end of May, and by mid-June the island is busy between 11:00 and 16:00. Mornings before 10:30 and evenings after the last day-trippers leave are still calm.

### July and August: Peak Season
These are the two crowded months. Jadrolinija line 807 runs 4 or 5 journeys per day in high season, and boat tours, speedboats and private yachts add to the numbers. Šunj Beach, on the island's southern side about 20–25 minutes' walk from the harbour, is the most crowded spot. Sunbed prices rise, and tables at waterfront restaurants need booking for dinner. The main dip is after about 17:00, when the day-trippers head back.

### September: Crowds Fall Through the Month
The first half of September is still lively. The timetable moves to its shoulder version from 31 August, and the island thins out noticeably from about 15 September. The last two weeks combine open venues with quiet beaches.

### October to December: Quiet Again
The off-season ferry timetable returns on 28 September. Visitors in October are few, and by November most seasonal businesses have closed. Only a handful of places stay open through winter.

## Best Times of Day and Week to Avoid Crowds

- **Arrive on the first ferry.** The first Dubrovnik departure is at 10:00 in the off-season and shoulder season, which puts you on Lopud before the speedboat tours land.
- **Go midweek.** Tuesday to Thursday is usually calmer than weekends, when locals and Dubrovnik residents also visit.
- **Stay overnight.** Day-trippers head back on the late-afternoon departures. After that, the harbour promenade and the Franciscan monastery area are close to empty.
- **Walk, don't sit on the main beach.** The path to Šunj takes about 20–25 minutes, and the far end of the bay is usually less crowded than the area near the beach bar.

## Local Tips

The sandy beach is the first thing most visitors look for, and it is also the most crowded place in July and August. The better plan in peak season is to skip it between 12:00 and 15:00. Walk uphill to the Fort Sutvrać viewpoint instead, or swim from the rocky coves along the main waterfront path. Avoiding Šunj at midday in August saves more hassle than any other decision on the island.

The ferry fare from Dubrovnik is low, so a late-day arrival on the afternoon departure is a cheap way to see the island after the crowds have left. Check the return times first, because the last departures are early.

## Quick Planning Summary

- Quietest with services open: May and late September
- Avoid if you dislike crowds: July and August, 11:00–16:00
- Empty but limited: November to March

faq.question: What is the busiest month in Lopud?
faq.answer: August is the busiest month, closely followed by July. Day-trippers from Dubrovnik, boat tours and yachts fill Šunj Beach and the harbour restaurants between about 11:00 and 16:00.

faq.question: When is Lopud least crowded?
faq.answer: November to March is the quietest period, but many restaurants and shops are closed and the ferry timetable is reduced. For low crowds with services open, May and the second half of September are better choices.

faq.question: How can I avoid crowds on Lopud in summer?
faq.answer: Take the first morning ferry, visit Tuesday to Thursday and stay overnight so you are on the island after the day-trippers leave. Avoid Šunj Beach between 12:00 and 15:00.

faq.question: Is Lopud crowded in June and September?
faq.answer: June is busy at midday, but mornings and evenings stay calm. September is moderately busy in the first half and quiet from about mid-month.

quickAnswer: Lopud is busiest from July to August, when day-trippers fill Šunj Beach and the ferries. June and September are moderately busy. The quietest months are November to March, when many businesses close. For a mix of open services and space, choose May or the last two weeks of September. Visit midweek and stay overnight.
